A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of CD44v isoforms may be used as a marker of cancer progression, and that CD44v isoform expression may be regulated by chemotherapy.

CD44v8–10 expression in cancer cells may be a potential marker for predicting the response of tumors to chemotherapy and for monitoring the recurrence of cancers in patients who are genetically predisposed to develop cancer.

the ectopic upregulation of CD44 may be a useful indicator of the development of resistance to chemotherapy in LFS.
